title: House History Pack
user: A homeowner who needs one durable history of appliances, seasonal work, repairs, warranties, permits, and contractor notes that can be handed to a buyer or service person.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The HN prompt asks what personal chore people automated, what they did manually before, and whether the automation remains dependable, highlighting continuing home-admin repetition.
A home-maintenance user requests an exportable PDF report and specifically wants permit documents included.

recurrence: Two 2026 discussions identify repeated personal administration and an explicit need to export home-maintenance evidence; losing history has financial and resale consequences.
current_workaround: Folders of receipts/manuals, email search, a calendar reminder, a spreadsheet, or starting a new note for every repair.
incumbents_and_gap: HomeZada, Centriq, and HomeBinder offer broad home platforms, often with accounts, marketplaces, or cloud lock-in. The gap is a local property record whose portable report is the primary artifact.
smallest_useful_product: An offline PWA for assets, service events, next-due tasks, warranty expiry, attached local files, and a selectable PDF/ZIP house-history pack.
success_measure: In a six-month pilot, 70% of users record at least five assets and can generate a complete maintenance packet for a chosen appliance in under two minutes.
constraints: Store sensitive files locally by default, provide encrypted export, use jurisdiction-neutral reports, and respect document copyright.
why_distinct: The core deliverable is a portable proof/history pack, not a generic task reminder app.
